D1.rationale: Computer-generated randomization with allocation performed by an independent coordinator using sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes, and no baseline imbalance (Table 1); signalling questions 1.1 = Y, 1.2 = Y, 1.3 = N, giving low risk by the algorithm.

D2.rationale: Treating physicians were necessarily unblinded (2.2 = Y), but no protocol deviations arising from the trial context were reported (2.3 = N, no crossovers permitted) and all 124 randomized patients were analysed in their assigned groups (2.6 = Y), so the algorithm yields low risk of bias for the effect of assignment.

D3.rationale: All 124 randomized patients completed the study and the 28-day mortality result is reported with the full denominators (62 vs 62), so outcome data were available for all participants (3.1 = Y); the conditional questions are not applicable.

D4.rationale: All-cause 28-day mortality is an objective outcome measured identically in both groups by assessors who remained blinded to allocation (4.1 = N, 4.2 = N, 4.3 = N), so knowledge of allocation is unlikely to have influenced its assessment.

D5.rationale: No protocol, statistical analysis plan or registry record is available, so pre-specification of the analysis could not be verified and questions 5.1, 5.2 and 5.3 were all answered NI; the algorithm for Domain 5 yields 'Some concerns' when the analysis intentions are not available.

overall.rationale: Domains 1 to 4 are at low risk of bias, but Domain 5 raises some concerns because the analysis was not shown to be pre-specified in any available document (5.1-5.3 = NI) and the reported result may therefore have been selected; one domain with some concerns gives an overall judgement of 'Some concerns'.

4.5.support: The same objective weaning criteria ('for 24 consecutive hours: PaO2/FiO2 ratio > 200 mmHg, PEEP <= 8 cmH2O, FiO2 <= 0.5, pH > 7.30, and respiratory rate <= 35 breaths/min') were applied in both groups, so there is no strong reason to believe that knowledge of allocation actually influenced the extubation decisions.

5.3.support: Analysis intentions are not available and the report does not show that the analysis of ventilation duration was pre-specified, so selection among possible analyses cannot be assessed.

D1.rationale: Computer-generated randomization with allocation performed by an independent coordinator using sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes, and no baseline imbalance (Table 1); signalling questions 1.1 = Y, 1.2 = Y, 1.3 = N, giving low risk by the algorithm.

D2.rationale: Treating physicians were necessarily unblinded (2.2 = Y), but no protocol deviations arising from the trial context were reported (2.3 = N, no crossovers permitted) and all 124 randomized patients were analysed in their assigned groups (2.6 = Y), so the algorithm yields low risk of bias for the effect of assignment.

D3.rationale: All 124 randomized patients completed the study and duration of ventilation is reported with the full denominators (62 vs 62), so outcome data were available for all participants (3.1 = Y); the conditional questions are not applicable.

D4.rationale: The measurement method and ascertainment were comparable between groups (4.1 = N, 4.2 = PN), but duration of ventilation is an intervention-provider decision outcome determined by an unblinded clinical team (4.3 = PY, 4.4 = PY); because the same objective weaning criteria were applied in both groups it is probably not the case that the assessment was influenced (4.5 = PN), which gives 'Some concerns' per the algorithm.

D5.rationale: No protocol, statistical analysis plan or registry record is available, so pre-specification of the analysis could not be verified and questions 5.1, 5.2 and 5.3 were all answered NI; the algorithm for Domain 5 yields 'Some concerns' when the analysis intentions are not available.

overall.rationale: Domains 1 to 3 are at low risk of bias, but Domain 4 raises some concerns because the duration of ventilation depends on extubation decisions made by an unblinded clinical team, and Domain 5 raises some concerns because no pre-specified analysis plan was available; two domains with some concerns give an overall judgement of 'Some concerns'.
